questions.stem: What are the products of the complete combustion of an alkane?
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of an alkane in excess oxygen produces carbon dioxide and water. For example, methane: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. Incomplete combustion (with limited oxygen) produces carbon monoxide or carbon (soot) instead.

questions.stem: Why do the boiling points of alkanes increase as the chain length increases?

options.text: The covalent bonds within the molecules become stronger
Larger molecules have stronger London dispersion forces between them
Longer chains form more hydrogen bonds

questions.explanation: Larger alkane molecules have more electrons and a greater surface area, leading to stronger London dispersion forces (van der Waals forces) between molecules. More energy is needed to overcome these stronger intermolecular forces, so the boiling point increases.
